# Social Circles Network Generator in Julia

This repository contains the code accompanying the following peer-reviewed paper:

> Chueca Del Cerro, C. and Badham, J. (2025). Tunable Network Properties with Hamill and Gilbert's Social Circles Generator. *Applied Network Science*. [DOI]( https://doi.org/10.1007/s41109-025-00744-5)

The Social Circles model is a spatially-embedded network generation algorithm originally proposed by Hamill and Gilbert (2009) in NetLogo, in which agents form connections based on overlapping social circles of varying reach within a population space.

> Hamill, L. and Gilbert, N. (2009). Social Circles: A Simple Structure for Agent-Based Social Network Models. *Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation*, 12(2), 3. https://www.jasss.org/12/2/3.html

This project re-implements the Social Circles model in Julia and substantially expands the original experimental design to assess its suitability as a generalisable network generator for social simulation research. Specifically, we extended the original parameter space to include a wider range of social reach values and population composition scenarios and we measured a broader set of structural network properties than the original study.

## Research Objectives

- Re-implement the Social Circles algorithm in Julia for performance and reproducibility.
- Expand the original experimental design to cover a wider range of social reach and population composition parameters.
- Measure and analyse a comprehensive set of structural network properties across the expanded parameter space.
- Evaluate the tunability and generalisability of the Social Circles model as a network generator.

## Repository Structure
├── LICENSE

├── README.md

├── Social_Circles.jl # Algorithm description and implementation

├── experimental_setup.jl # experimental set up and simulation

├── SC_analyses.R # data analyses and visualisation 

## Key Findings

While Social Circles generates networks with high clustering coefficient, positive degree assortativity and short path lengths, these properties are tightly associated so the algorithm could not be used to target specific combinations of properties without additional steps.

## How to Run

### Prerequisites
Julia 1.x or above. Install required packages:

```julia
using Pkg
Pkg.add(["Graphs", "Random", "Statistics", "DataFrames", "StatsBase", "Inequality", "CSV", "OrderedCollections", "Distributions"])
```

### Reproducing the Experiments & Results 

```julia
# Step 1: import the network generator
include("Social_Circles.jl")

# Step 2: import the network property calculator
include("github.com/chuecadelc/NetGenerators/Network_properties.jl")

# Step 3: run the desired experiments given the set of parameters
 Social_Circles_Proportions(rows,cols,population,proportions[1],proportions[2],social_distances[sr])
```

```R
# Step 4: Run this script to reproduce the data analyses and figures
include("SC_analyses.R")
```

Note: Experiments were conducted on a high-performance computing (HPC) environment running Linux due to the size of the experimental set up and the network.
